sources.title: CMA opens investigation into Meta's commercial terms, October 30, 2026
Meta commercial terms case, opened October 30, 2026

title: UK competition regulator opens a case into Meta's business terms
dek: The CMA will examine whether Meta's terms let it reuse publishers' website content, including for AI features, without giving them a choice.
lede: Britain's Competition and Markets Authority opened a formal investigation on October 30 into Meta's commercial terms for businesses. The regulator wants to know whether those terms let Meta reuse publishers' website content, including for AI features, without a real choice.

facts.label: Question
facts.value: Possible abuse of a dominant position

body.text: The concern is specific. Meta's revised terms for businesses could let the company use content from publishers' websites in its own products, AI features included. According to the CMA, publishers would not get to choose whether that reuse happens.

body.heading: Meta has already pressed pause
body.text: Meta paused the revised terms on October 28 to consult the industry, the CMA says. It had already delayed their introduction once. The pause does not end the case: the regulator will still assess whether Meta holds a dominant position and whether the terms abuse it.

body.heading: What happens next
body.text: The official timetable puts information gathering first and runs it until January 2027. The CMA says those dates may move. Opening a case is not a finding, and the regulator has said plainly that no infringement has been established.

For publishers, the case tests a trade-off many already live with. They reach readers through a platform, and they accept whatever reuse the platform's contract allows. A decision against Meta could strengthen their hand in those negotiations.

buildersNote: If your product takes in content through platform partnerships, check where your rights come from: the platform's contract or the publisher's consent. This case turns on exactly that difference, and the answer may change which platform data you can use for AI.
